title: The text discusses the impact of agricultural mechanization and the Green Revolution on small-scale farmers in Africa. It highlights how multinational corporations, in collaboration with organizations like the FAO, promote mechanization and chemical inputs, which are often unaffordable for small peasants. The shift towards cash crops, driven by government policies and World Bank influence, has led to a decline in traditional grain production, resulting in food insecurity. The text also illustrates the negative consequences of these policies, such as increased taxes on peasants and environmental degradation, particularly in regions like the Sahel, which once thrived on traditional agriculture but now faces desertification due to unsustainable practices.
